prompt: Four replicas average 90% CPU utilisation against a target of 60%. How many replicas does the autoscaler ask for?

The load pushed utilisation to 604% and the replicas stopped at 6. Why not more?

choices.why: All six ran; no pod was `Pending`.
Right. The formula asked for more and was capped.
It gave far more than 6 at that reading.

prompt: Right after the HPA was created, its events said `no metrics returned`. What did it do with the replicas?

choices.text: It scaled to the maximum to be safe
choices.why: That is not the safe direction it takes.

prompt: By default, why does the autoscaler wait before removing replicas after the load drops?

choices.text: Pods take five minutes to stop
choices.why: Stopping is quick; the wait is a choice.

choices.text: It uses the highest recommendation of the last five minutes
choices.why: Right, so a brief dip does not remove pods needed again soon.
It reports every fifteen seconds either way.

prompt: Why is memory often a poor metric to scale a web service on?
hint: What happens to memory when the load goes?

choices.why: Utilisation is a percentage either way.

choices.text: It seldom falls after the load ends
choices.why: Right. The autoscaler then scales up and never back down.
